access_continuity_justification: Not yet met: only one person can merge and release. Mitigations are documented (the MIT license allows an immediate fork; release provenance is designed to use keyless signing, so no private signing material is needed to build or verify a release), and a co-maintainer is the preferred remedy; neither a co-maintainer nor credential escrow is arranged yet. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: Today's output is plain text, with no color and no cursor control. The design requires that color is never the only carrier of meaning (state words or symbols too), that NO_COLOR is honored, and that the planned web interface meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and is keyboard navigable.
achieve_passing_justification: The project is not registered for the badge yet. Reaching "passing" is planned for the first release (0.1.0).
assurance_case_justification: Not yet: docs/threat-model.md describes the assets, threat sources, trust boundaries, the controls with their status (in place or designed) and the residual risks, but the assurance case (secure design principles and common weaknesses countered, each with evidence) is planned for the first release. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: CI is configured to run the whole test suite in GitHub Actions on every push to main and every pull request, and reports success or failure per check. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_common_tools_justification: The standard Go toolchain (go build, go test).
build_floss_tools_justification: The binaries build with the Go toolchain alone, which is FLOSS. The checks also use FLOSS tools (golangci-lint, govulncheck, actionlint, go-licenses, zizmor, OpenSSF Scorecard), except CodeQL: its query packs are open source, but its analysis engine is free for open source projects without being FLOSS, and nothing in the build depends on it.
build_justification: Standard Go build: go build ./cmd/irekey (documented in the README); CI is configured to build every target on every change. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/README.md#building-from-source
build_non_recursive_justification: The Go toolchain builds from the full package dependency graph; there is no recursive build system.
build_preserve_debug_justification: A plain go build keeps the debugging information. Only the CI build job strips its binaries (-s -w), on purpose and visibly in the workflow, and so does the executor size guard, which builds a stripped executor only to measure it. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_repeatable_justification: Not yet: there is no release to rebuild. Reproducible release builds (CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, the version set with -ldflags, SHA256SUMS) and a CI job that rebuilds a released tag and compares the checksums are planned with the release workflow.
build_standard_variables_justification: The build is the plain Go toolchain (go build), which honors the standard Go environment variables (GOFLAGS, GOOS, GOARCH, GOARM and the CGO_* variables); no build script overrides them. irekey has no C code, so no C compiler or C flags are involved; the CI builds set CGO_ENABLED=0.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 (single maintainer), as stated in GOVERNANCE.md. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
code_of_conduct_justification: Contributor Covenant 2.1, in the standard location. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: gofmt and golangci-lint (configured in .golangci.yml) run in the CI lint job on every push to main and every pull request; the job fails on any finding, and lint is a required check for every merge to main. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.golangci.yml
coding_standards_justification: Effective Go and the Go Code Review Comments, gofmt and the repository's golangci-lint configuration, plus project rules (error wrapping, context and timeouts, structured redacted logging, no unsafe or cgo, SPDX headers). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes the contribution process: development setup, the checks to run before a pull request, the rules, and squash-merged pull requests. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements for acceptable contributions (tests required, English only, no real-world data, dependency justification, Conventional Commits, SHA-pinned actions, changelog, decision records), the pull request template has the checklist, and GOVERNANCE.md lists the feature acceptance criteria. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none. The design uses SSH through golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, which negotiates its algorithms, and OpenSSH-format signatures (SSHSIG), which name their key and hash algorithms; this answer will be revised when that code exists.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none. The design calls existing libraries (golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, filippo.io/age and an SSHSIG implementation) and forbids custom cryptography.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: irekey does not use TLS yet. The designed forge integrations use HTTPS; this answer will be revised when they exist.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: irekey processes no credentials yet. In the design, device credentials are references into a vault (an age-encrypted file or Bitwarden), kept apart from code and configuration, and SSH keys stay in the user's agent or key files.
crypto_floss_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none. The designed libraries (golang.org/x/crypto, filippo.io/age) are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none. The design uses the user's existing SSH keys and the defaults of golang.org/x/crypto/ssh and age.
crypto_password_storage_justification: irekey does not authenticate users and stores no passwords for that purpose. In the design, device passwords live only in the vault (an age-encrypted file or Bitwarden), never in the repository.
crypto_pfs_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none. The design uses SSH, whose key exchange provides perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_published_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none. The design uses only published protocols and formats: SSH, the OpenSSH signature format, age and SHA-256.
crypto_random_justification: irekey generates no keys or nonces yet. The design generates per-update keys and session tokens with a cryptographically secure generator.
crypto_tls12_justification: irekey does not use TLS yet.
crypto_used_network_justification: irekey opens no network connection yet. The design uses only SSH to devices and HTTPS to forges, and no unencrypted protocol.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: irekey does not use TLS yet.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none. The design uses no algorithm with known serious weaknesses (SHA-256 for digests, SSH and SSHSIG with the user's keys).
crypto_working_justification: No cryptography is implemented yet: the two existing commands use none.
dco_justification: Contributions require a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off (git commit -s); the dco job in CI fails a pull request when one of its commits has no sign-off. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
delivery_mitm_justification: The source is delivered over HTTPS or SSH from GitHub. There is no release yet; releases are planned on GitHub over HTTPS, with SHA256SUMS and build provenance attestations (Sigstore).
delivery_unsigned_justification: Nothing is published over plain HTTP. Checksums of the planned releases are to be published only on GitHub over HTTPS, together with a signed provenance attestation.
dependency_monitoring_justification: govulncheck is configured to run on every change; GitHub Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled, and Dependabot proposes updates for Go modules and GitHub Actions weekly. Today the module has no dependency outside the standard library. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: The README starts by stating what irekey does: it manages the same software running on many offline embedded Linux computers, where every customer needs small local differences, and delivers changes over SSH with automatic rollback. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/README.md
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/issues
documentation_achievements_justification: No achievement has been attained yet. The README shows the OpenSSF Scorecard badge; the OpenSSF Best Practices badge will be added after the project is registered.
documentation_architecture_justification: The specification describes the architecture: the zones (operator machine, device, forge), the architectural decisions, the repository layout and the package dependency rule; docs/adr records each decision. A separate docs/architecture.md is planned. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/docs/spec/masterprompt.md
documentation_basics_justification: The README states the status, what irekey is for and not for, and how to build and run what exists today; the specification documents the whole design. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: Pull requests that change behavior update the README, the docs, the specification and the changelog in the same pull request, as the pull request template requires; the README states which parts are designed and not implemented yet. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
documentation_interface_justification: Today the external interface is two commands, irekey version and irekey-exec capabilities, documented in the README and printed by their --help. The planned command line, exit codes and error model are specified in the specification. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/docs/spec/masterprompt.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: Not yet: the README has a planned quick start, marked as not working yet, for the first release. Today the only working steps are building from source and running irekey version. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/README.md#planned-quick-start
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md covers October 2026 to October 2027 (Now, Next, Later), including what is not planned. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md states what users can and cannot expect, separating what holds today from what the design commits to; docs/threat-model.md gives the status of every control. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-model-what-you-can-and-cannot-expect
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The Go runtime always checks bounds, nil dereferences and type assertions; CI is configured to run the test suite with the race detector, which instruments memory accesses (the fuzzers run without it).
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Dynamic analysis has not reported any vulnerability yet; there is no release.
dynamic_analysis_justification: CI is configured to run the whole test suite with the race detector, and native Go fuzzing for 30 seconds per target on every change and 5 minutes per target weekly. Today the fuzz targets cover the parsers of the repository guards; fuzz targets for irekey's own parsers (bundle manifest, journal, device output) come with that code. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: irekey is written in Go, a memory-safe language, and uses neither cgo nor the unsafe package; an architecture test fails if any package imports unsafe or C.
english_justification: All documentation, code, messages and discussion are in English; a CI guard rejects non-ASCII letters outside the files that explain the project's name and the test fixtures for UTF-8 handling.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been filed yet; requests will be answered per GOVERNANCE.md, which states the acceptance criteria.
external_dependencies_justification: go.mod lists every dependency; today there is none outside the standard library. Every future module must also be listed, with its license, in scripts/guard/allowed-modules.txt. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/go.mod
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents how decisions are made: a single maintainer decides, in public issues and pull requests, against written acceptance criteria, and design changes get an architecture decision record. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#decision-making
hardening_justification: Go provides mandatory bounds and nil checks and a memory-safe runtime; CI builds static binaries with CGO_ENABLED=0; an architecture test forbids unsafe and cgo in every package; the executor depends on no operator-side package and on nothing outside the standard library and this module. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: Not yet: the design applies fail-safe defaults, least privilege, complete mediation, economy of mechanism and defense in depth (see docs/threat-model.md), but most of it is not implemented. The code that exists follows it (the executor depends on nothing outside the standard library and this module, and contains no network code). The assurance case that argues the design is planned for the first release.
input_validation_justification: Today the only input is the command line: both binaries accept only their known commands and reject any extra argument, which the tests cover. The design validates every deployment repository file against a JSON Schema (unknown keys are errors) and parses device output strictly, with size limits.
installation_common_justification: Not yet: there is no release. Building from source is documented in the README; static release binaries with checksums are planned for the first release, and packages for Homebrew, Scoop, winget, .deb and .rpm after it.
installation_development_quick_justifica: Clone the repository and run go test ./...: the Go toolchain (and git) is all that is needed, and go.mod selects the toolchain version. A C compiler is needed only for the race detector. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development-setup
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no installation system yet; a built binary is a single file that the user places where they choose.
interact_justification: The README explains how to obtain the source, how to report security issues, and how to contribute (CONTRIBUTING.md, pull requests). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/README.md
interfaces_current_justification: staticcheck (part of golangci-lint's standard linters) reports uses of deprecated APIs, and the CI lint job fails on any finding.
internationalization_justification: All interface text is English and is not externalized for translation. Localization beyond English is an open question in the specification.
know_common_errors_justification: The design counters the common errors of this kind of software: path traversal and unsafe archive entries (bundle path checks, fuzzed), command injection (remote commands from an argument vector with one tested quoting function, and a CI guard), disabled host-key verification (pinning, and a CI guard), secrets in cleartext or in logs (vault references and redaction of every writer), resource exhaustion from device output (size limits), and memory safety (Go, no cgo, no unsafe). See docs/threat-model.md.
know_secure_design_justification: The design applies fail-safe defaults (an unclassified error aborts before the switch and rolls back after it; unknown is not success), least privilege (only the executor runs under sudo; it never listens on a port or initiates network connections; whether its health checks may reach the device's own services on loopback is an open question), complete mediation (every connection checks the pinned host key; every bundle is verified on the device), economy of mechanism (standard library first) and defense in depth (approval, signing and device binding). See docs/threat-model.md.
license_location_justification: The license is in the LICENSE file at the repository root. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/LICENSE
maintained_justification: The project is in active early development; see the commit history and the open pull requests. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/commits/main
maintenance_or_update_justification: No version has been released yet. STABILITY.md defines the upgrade path from 1.0 on: contracts, deprecation for at least two minor versions, and a migration command for deployment repository formats.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds no credentials; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled, and a CI guard rejects real-world addresses.
regression_tests_added50_justification: No bug has been fixed yet. The rules require a regression test for every bug fix (CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template).
release_notes_justification: Not yet: there is no release. CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog) keeps an Unreleased section, and the planned release workflow is designed to fail when a version has no changelog section and to publish that section as the release notes. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: There is no release, and no publicly known vulnerability has been fixed; the changelog has a Security section for future fixes.
repo_interim_justification: Interim work is public: changes are proposed as pull requests to main, visible before and after they are merged. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/pulls?q=is%3Apr
repo_track_justification: Git records each change, its author and its date; after the bootstrap commit, changes are proposed as pull requests.
report_archive_justification: The GitHub issue tracker keeps a public, searchable archive of reports and responses. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported through GitHub issues, with a bug report form. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been filed yet.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists the roles (maintainer, reviewer, security responder, release manager, code of conduct enforcement), their responsibilities and who holds each. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
signed_releases_justification: Not yet: there is no release. Planned: Sigstore build provenance attestations for every binary and SBOM (keyless, so no private key is stored), and version tags signed with the maintainer's SSH key, whose public half is in .github/allowed_signers.
sites_https_justification: The project site, repository and downloads are on GitHub over HTTPS: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub and, once registered, bestpractices.dev; the project stores no passwords itself.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: gosec and CodeQL's security-extended queries look for common vulnerability patterns; govulncheck checks the code and the standard library against the Go vulnerability database.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No medium or higher severity vulnerability has been found by static analysis. golangci-lint v2.14.0, gosec included, reports zero issues on the current code (checked locally), and the required lint check fails any pull request with a finding; CodeQL reports its findings to GitHub code scanning.
static_analysis_justification: golangci-lint (the standard linters, which include staticcheck and govet, plus gosec, errorlint and others), govulncheck and CodeQL with the security-extended queries are configured to run on every push to main and every pull request. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis is configured to run on every push to main and every pull request, and CodeQL also weekly.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions is configured to run lint, the guards, vet, race-enabled tests with a coverage floor, short fuzzing, a vulnerability check, the license check and cross-platform builds on every push to main and every pull request. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: go test ./... (the standard Go invocation; documented in the README and CONTRIBUTING.md). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#before-opening-a-pull-request
test_justification: An automated test suite (go test) covers both commands, the version package, the package dependency rules (architecture tests), the schema version list and every repository guard. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#before-opening-a-pull-request
test_most_justification: Statement coverage of the product code (the packages under cmd/ and internal/) is 96.4% (go test -coverpkg=./cmd/...,./internal/..., measured locally on the current code): the code of the two binaries and of the version and schema packages is fully covered, except the one-line main functions. The guard program in scripts/ is tested as well but not counted.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: every change comes with tests in the same pull request, and a bug fix comes with a regression test that fails without the fix. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: every change comes with tests in the same pull request; every safety invariant has tests named after it. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage of the product code (the packages under cmd/ and internal/) is 96.4% (go test -coverpkg=./cmd/...,./internal/..., measured locally); the required test check fails when it is below 80%. The guard program in scripts/ is tested as well but not counted. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
tests_are_added_justification: The first code change, the Go module with irekey version and irekey-exec capabilities, added tests for both commands, the version package, the architecture rules, the schema version list and every guard, each guard with passing and failing fixtures.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test policy is in CONTRIBUTING.md and in the checklist of the pull request template. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All reused components are Go modules managed by go.mod (none outside the standard library yet); there are no vendored or forked copies.
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, as stated in CHANGELOG.md and STABILITY.md.
version_tags_justification: Not yet: there is no release and no version tag. Each release is planned to be identified by a signed annotated git tag (vX.Y.Z); a repository ruleset already prevents v* tags from being deleted, moved or updated.
version_tags_signed_justification: Not yet: there is no version tag. Version tags are to be signed with git tag -s and verified against the SSH key in .github/allowed_signers.
version_unique_justification: Not yet: there is no release. Each release will have a unique version, starting with 0.1.0.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known critical vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no publicly known vulnerabilities; govulncheck is configured to run on every change.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability has been reported or resolved; SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-we-handle-a-report
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md describes how to report vulnerabilities. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received; SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgement within 5 business days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents how reports are handled: acknowledgement, assessment, a fix in a private advisory fork with a regression test, the advisory with a CVE when one applies, and credit. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-we-handle-a-report
warnings_fixed_justification: go vet and golangci-lint report zero findings on the current code (checked locally); CI is configured to fail on any finding.
warnings_justification: go vet and golangci-lint (the standard linters plus bodyclose, contextcheck, errname, errorlint, exhaustive, gocritic, gosec, noctx and revive) are configured to run in CI. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/irekey/blob/main/.golangci.yml
warnings_strict_justification: golangci-lint runs the standard set plus nine more linters, including gosec and revive. The exclusions are few and each is explained: gosec in _test.go files (in .golangci.yml: fixtures use fixed modes and temporary paths), and three inline gosec G204 exclusions in the guard tooling, which runs the fixed git and go programs.
